name: Gwion

attributes.attribute: The first incarnation of the great bard Taliesin.
Hired by Ceridwen, he stirred her cauldron for a year and a day.
He absorbed the wisdom meant for Ceridwen's son.
Pursued Gwion through a series of transformations.
Reborn from Ceridwen and became the bard Taliesin.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gwion Bach is the name of a servant in the Hanes Taliesin, the tale of the poet Taliesin. That servant gains the gift of poetic inspiration meant for Morfran. The poet's mother figure, the shape-shifting goddess Ceridwen, was to brew a cauldron of wisdom. Three drops fell on Gwion instead, so the power passed to him. The angry goddess then chased him through many changes of form. In the end she swallowed him and later gave birth to him anew. That reborn child became the great poet Taliesin. Gwion's many transformations are often set beside those of Tuan mac Cairill. So a humble servant rises to become the master of Welsh poetry.

okr.objective: Trace Gwion from cauldron servant to the reborn bard Taliesin.
